items.originalTitle: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
items.summary: Five people have been killed and 16 injured in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.

evidenceRecords.text: At least five people were killed and 16 wounded Thursday in a Houthi missile and drone attack on the palace located in Yemen's interim capital – the southern port city of Aden, used by the country's internationally recognised government, an official said.

AFP also reported that a Yemeni government minister said on condition of anonymity on Thursday that a Houthi missile attack on the presidential palace in Aden had hit a command center for the Saudi-led coalition.

The official added that the command center was hit by three missiles, and the headquarters of the coalition forces at the presidential complex with two missiles, adding that there were Yemeni and Saudi casualties, without providing a specific toll.
There was no immediate confirmation of the report that the prime minister was in the presidential palace at the time of Houthi attack.
Many of Yemen’s government leaders are living in exile, and those in Aden were safe, a government official told the AP.

The Houthis said they attacked a military operations headquarters with the “Saudi enemy”, part of their strategy of attacking Saudi targets that has included a series of attacks on airports and oil infrastructure inside the kingdom.
Earlier on Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted a cruise missile over the province of Medina.
Flightradar24, a tracking platform, said dozens of flights were canceled or delayed at Jeddah’s airport.
The coalition statement did not assign blame for the attack.
The Houthis’ military spokesperson, Brig Gen Yahya Saree, denied the rebels carried it out.
The group previously pledged not to attack airports in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina in Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia also said it destroyed a drone over the country’s eastern province, a major oil-producing region, and intercepted a drone in Khamis Mushait, near a major military airbase.
Earlier this week, Saudi Arabia said the headquarters of the oil giant Saudi Aramco were hit by Houthi attacks, and reported damage to the building.

items.title: France to go it alone on next-gen combat aircraft after FCAS collapse
items.originalTitle: France to go it alone on next-gen combat aircraft after FCAS collapse
items.summary: PARIS — France will develop a next-generation combat aircraft domestically as a successor to the Rafale, after a joint project with Germany and Spain for a future combat air system collapsed earlier this year, Air and Space Force Chief of Staff Jérôme Bellanger said. The country now conceives the future fighter, dubbed Avion de Combat du Futur or ACF, as a national project, with a target of flying conventional missions in 2040, Bellanger told the National Assembly’s defense committee in a hearing here on Wednesday.

evidenceRecords.text: PARIS — France will develop a next-generation combat aircraft domestically as a successor to the Rafale, after a joint project with Germany and Spain for a future combat air system collapsed earlier this year, Air and Space Force Chief of Staff Jérôme Bellanger said.

The country now conceives the future fighter, dubbed Avion de Combat du Futur or ACF, as a national project, with a target of flying conventional missions in 2040, Bellanger told the National Assembly’s defense committee in a hearing here on Wednesday.
“We’re now moving on to work that will prefigure and enable the birth of this ACF, this future combat aircraft as a national program,” Bellanger said.

France remains open to possible cooperation with other countries, “but within different frameworks and which won’t be structural to the birth of this aircraft.” France and Germany agreed to scrap the FCAS project in June, after years of wrangling about specifications and industrial control between Dassault Aviation and Airbus.

That’s left both countries without a clear successor for their existing fleets of Rafale and Eurofighter jets, respectively, though Germany has started receiving the first F-35 jets ordered in 2022 to replace the Panavia Tornado.

Dassault Aviation CEO Éric Trappier has said his company and France have all the know-how and skills to develop a next-generation fighter jet, together with engine partner Safran and defense-electronics firm Thales, and he would be able to do so “well below” a budget of €50 billion (US$56 billion).
All the years working on FCAS “haven’t been wasted,” with progress in areas including the aircraft, drones, stealth, connectivity and combat cloud, Bellanger said.
Work had been split up in several so-called pillars that also included a new engine, with Dassault and Airbus working on the next-gen fighter pillar at the heart of the system.
“The halt of the FCAS program doesn’t mean we’re throwing everything away,” Bellanger said.
“Our teams, the industrial teams have been working on the NGF, stealth, the cloud, and so on.

France will need to have a Rafale F5 standard in 2035 that incorporates the first components of the future combat aircraft, related to the engine, the sensors and the Stratus RS missile to neutralize enemy air defenses, according to Bellanger.

items.summary: The California-based defense company Kratos announced this week the first test flight of the uncrewed combat aircraft known as the U740 Valkyrie over European skies, as well as the first successful flight tests of a new turbojet engine designed for small aerial systems. The U740 Valkyrie was developed through a partnership with the Dutch company Airbus in support of German and other European armed forces. In a joint statement , Mike Schoellhorn, the chief executive of Airbus Defence and Space, explained that the Valkyrie combined Kratos’ low-cost airframe with Airbus’ sovereign European mission system. “In an increasingly complex and contested threat environment, air forces require affordable combat mass today,” he said, adding that the Valkyrie will also support crewed combat aircraft with extended range, firepower and survivability.

items.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
items.originalTitle: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
items.summary: Meta has launched what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States. Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs. The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday. Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and built for complex coding tasks and agentic labor. It has also been designed to run locally on Apple’s computers. However, you will still need a lot of power to run the model locally, with a requirement of at least 1 terabyte of RAM, per Engadget. The model will run best via the Mac Studio that comes equipped with the M5 Ultra chip. Still, if you can muster the memory, Muse Spark Open may prove a significant work horse for coding and other desktop tasks. Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.” The company says it also deployed it in the service of running DaVinci Resolve, the high-end video editing software, revealing that the model was capable of reviewing and cropping footage. Open-weight models provide a number of distinct industry advantages that aren’t afforded by closed and proprietary models.

deepread.lead: 机器人初创企业在传感、运动控制和AI上往往跑得很快，却在电子、系统集成、验证与制造环节卡住。ADI把Emerging Tech Hub放进Analog Garage，试图以弹性工程支持和制造资源弥合这段断层，但能否真正帮企业规模化，还取决于资源如何匹配不同阶段的需求。

chapters.title: ADI设机器人初创陪跑平台，能否补上量产断层

sentences.text: ADI高级产品技术经理卡梅伦·维隆把机器人初创企业当下最大的挑战归结为行业变化的速度。
在他看来，多数初创企业擅长采用传感、运动控制和AI等新一代技术，但商业化还需要电子、系统集成、验证和制造方面的额外专业能力。
这些需求往往会拉紧张小型工程团队的资源。
ADI正在Analog Garage内发展Emerging Tech Hub，面向机器人初创企业和成熟公司，帮助它们应对上述挑战。
据该机构披露，这个中心意在让企业在把设计推向生产前，获得ADI工程师、原型设计与测试资源以及制造和采购方面的专业能力。

sentences.text: Emerging Tech Hub被描述为一个聚焦机器人的计划，目标是把初创公司和成熟机器人企业拉近到ADI的技术团队，其中包括正在落地新发布或仍在开发中的技术的工程师。
ADI提供的工程支持将取决于机器人公司所处的阶段和具体需求。
例如，一家成熟机器人开发商可能需要某种特定的半导体元器件，另一家可能在解决不同的工程问题，Emerging Tech Hub便会在ADI内部寻找相应的专家。
维隆表示，ADI已从行业各处招募机器人专家，以便更好地应对快节奏的机器人开发。
ADI此前在一份白皮书中把物理AI描述为把传感、信号转换、感知、推理、控制、计算和验证结合在一起，并把它分为创意、原型、验证和规模化四个阶段。
ADI称，机器人初创企业不断变化的需求，正是Emerging Tech Hub想要填补的缺口。

sentences.text: 从机制上看，ADI要兜住的不是单点技术，而是从创意到规模化之间的工程化断层。
依据是ADI自己把物理AI拆成创意、原型、验证和规模化四个阶段，又承认初创企业在电子、系统集成、验证和制造上需要额外专业能力，这说明断层主要出在跨学科整合，而非算法或传感本身。
但这种模式的约束同样来自阶段差异：支持内容取决于企业所处阶段和需求，成熟开发商可能只要一颗特定元器件，另一家可能要解决完全不同的工程问题，这意味着中心更像一个按需求调配专家的接口，而不是一条标准化的量产服务流水线。
因此它能否奏效，关键不在于工程师数量，而在于匹配效率：若每次需求都要在ADI内部临时寻找专家，规模化的边际成本可能偏高。

evidenceRecords.text: “The biggest challenge I see robotics startups facing today is the speed at which the industry moves,” says Cameron Villone, Senior Product Technology Manager at Analog Devices Inc. (ADI).

In most cases, a startup excels in adopting next-generation technologies in sensing, motion control, and AI, but commercialization requires additional expertise in electronics, system integration, validation, and manufacturing.
These demands can often stretch the resources of smaller engineering teams.
ADI is developing its Emerging Tech Hub within the Analog Garage to help robotics startups and established companies overcome these challenges.
The Emerging Tech Hub is intended to give companies access to ADI engineers, prototyping and testing resources, and manufacturing and sourcing expertise as they prepare their designs for production.

The challenges of scaling robotics innovation ADI was recently highlighted in The Race to Make AI Physical whitepaper explaining how physical AI brings together sensing, signal conversion, perception, reasoning, control, computing, and validation.
ADI describes this through four stages: Idea, Prototype, Validate, and Scale.
These changing demands for a robotics startup are the gaps ADI’s Emerging Tech Hub is intended to address.

The Emerging Tech Hub brings expertise and resources The Emerging Tech Hub is a robotics-focused initiative being developed to bring startups and established robotics companies closer to ADI’s technical teams, including engineers implementing newly released or still-in-development technologies.
The engineering support from ADI will depend on the robotics company’s stage and needs.

For example, a mature robotics developer might need a particular semiconductor component, while another may be trying to solve a different engineering problem, prompting the Emerging Tech Hub to find specialists within ADI.
Villone said ADI has recruited robotics experts from across the industry to be better equipped to handle fast paced robotic development.

evidenceRecords.text: After eight months aboard the International Space Station, NASA and SpaceX’s Crew-12 mission is scheduled to undock from the Station’s Harmony port on Oct. 7 to return to Earth.
Undocking and landing Crew-12 is scheduled to undock from the International Space Station’s (ISS) Harmony zenith port on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at 12:05 UTC (08:05 EDT).

Crew-12’s crew spent their last days on the Station preparing for their return, packing essential items, testing their SpaceX pressure suits, and preparing the Station for the arrival of their follow-up mission, Crew-13.
Expedition 75 crew members onboard the Station will then work to ensure Crew-12 can safely undock from the ISS, checking pressure values and hatch seals.
The crew of Crew-12 don their SpaceX pressure suits in preparation for undocking.
Crew-12 launched to the ISS on Feb. 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.
Crew-12’s return was greenlit by the arrival of Crew-13 on Oct. 1 at 23:05 UTC.
Crew-12 marks Crew Dragon Freedom’s fifth mission overall, following Crew-4, Crew-9, Axiom-2, and Axiom-3.
When Freedom splashes down with Crew-12, it will have spent a total of 609 days and 11 hours in space.

history.title: NASA Seeks US Industry Plans for Commercial Space Stations
history.originalTitle: NASA Seeks US Industry Plans for Commercial Space Stations

evidenceRecords.text: Credit: NASA NASA is advancing American leadership in space by taking the next step toward a future where commercial space stations lead the way in low Earth orbit.
On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations.

“In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.

Commercial space stations may provide that capability while creating new opportunities for American industry and allowing NASA to concentrate more of our resources on the near-impossible missions ahead.” Building on the agency’s Ignition event earlier this year, NASA regularly has engaged with private industry to shape the agency’s future direction in low Earth orbit.
This included publishing two Requests for Information in March to gather industry’s perspective on low Earth orbit destinations and transportation.

The agency also published a draft Request for Proposals in July, followed by an industry day and one-on-one meetings that allowed interested companies to review and comment on the planned acquisition approach.
“We’ve made it clear that NASA will never give up its presence in low Earth orbit,” said Isaacman.
“Since Ignition, we have spent a lot of time listening to industry and working through what it will take to make this transition successful.

We want to see credible plans, strong technical execution, and companies prepared to invest in destinations that can serve NASA while developing additional customers and markets of their own.” Proposals are due Tuesday, Dec. 8, with contract awards expected in spring 2027.

Undocking and landing Crew-12 is scheduled to undock from the International Space Station’s (ISS) Harmony zenith port on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at 12:05 UTC (08:05 EDT).

Crew-12’s crew spent their last days on the Station preparing for their return, packing essential items, testing their SpaceX pressure suits, and preparing the Station for the arrival of their follow-up mission, Crew-13.
Expedition 75 crew members onboard the Station will then work to ensure Crew-12 can safely undock from the ISS, checking pressure values and hatch seals.
The crew of Crew-12 don their SpaceX pressure suits in preparation for undocking.
Crew-12 launched to the ISS on Feb. 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.
Crew-12’s return was greenlit by the arrival of Crew-13 on Oct. 1 at 23:05 UTC.
Crew-12 marks Crew Dragon Freedom’s fifth mission overall, following Crew-4, Crew-9, Axiom-2, and Axiom-3.
When Freedom splashes down with Crew-12, it will have spent a total of 609 days and 11 hours in space.

history.title: NASA Seeks US Industry Plans for Commercial Space Stations
history.originalTitle: NASA Seeks US Industry Plans for Commercial Space Stations

evidenceRecords.text: Credit: NASA NASA is advancing American leadership in space by taking the next step toward a future where commercial space stations lead the way in low Earth orbit.
On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations.

“In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.

Commercial space stations may provide that capability while creating new opportunities for American industry and allowing NASA to concentrate more of our resources on the near-impossible missions ahead.” Building on the agency’s Ignition event earlier this year, NASA regularly has engaged with private industry to shape the agency’s future direction in low Earth orbit.
This included publishing two Requests for Information in March to gather industry’s perspective on low Earth orbit destinations and transportation.

The agency also published a draft Request for Proposals in July, followed by an industry day and one-on-one meetings that allowed interested companies to review and comment on the planned acquisition approach.
“We’ve made it clear that NASA will never give up its presence in low Earth orbit,” said Isaacman.
“Since Ignition, we have spent a lot of time listening to industry and working through what it will take to make this transition successful.

We want to see credible plans, strong technical execution, and companies prepared to invest in destinations that can serve NASA while developing additional customers and markets of their own.” Proposals are due Tuesday, Dec. 8, with contract awards expected in spring 2027.
